hypothesis: When independent GFS and ECMWF IFS ensemble distributions agree on the direction and magnitude of a daily-temperature bucket mispricing, a fixed high-edge subset may retain positive settlement value after fees and model stress even though raw single-model ensemble forecasts generally do not beat the Kalshi market.
research_basis: Open-Meteo Ensemble API: NOAA GEFS 31-member and ECMWF IFS 51-member global ensembles
AwpDemon/kalshi-weather-bot: self-reported +$3.89 on 20 settled paper trades, too small and not independently auditable
wallyworley/weatherbot EXP-2026-013: all twelve ensemble variants lost to the Kalshi market on Brier and ranked probability score over 578 station-days and 19 stations
wallyworley/weatherbot EXP-2026-011: hobby-scale model-run latency was negative at full preregistered power

universe.contract_type: registered Kalshi daily high and low temperature ladders

forecast.forecast_vintage_rule: first observed receipt time; provider run labels are not used as availability timestamps
forecast.bias_correction: none until strictly prior station-season outcomes exist; raw ensemble is measured honestly

comparison.primary_benchmark: normalized Kalshi midpoint distribution on the same event and timestamp
